# Tracing Recurrent and Emergent Hallucination Patterns in Decomposed Text-to-SQL Generation

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#drilldown-hallucinations)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-13**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.uncertainlp-main.40.pdf) · UncertaiNLP 2026 proceedings, pages 672–682; 11-page workshop paper

**Reading coverage:** All 11 PDF pages: Sections 1–9, limitations, references, Appendices A–D, all six annotation-rule definitions, prompts, Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–3. Visually inspected the workflow, category distribution, conditional-probability plots and final execution table on PDF pages 3, 5, 6, 7 and 11. Separately inspected the paper-linked public artifact inventory and evaluation-script/annotation structure.

**Additional inspected sources:** [Paper-linked evaluation artifacts at inspected revision](https://github.com/HaydenMM/bird-mini-drilldown/tree/9050803cada1a0750d783685a2508c95fc45e3b0)

## Research question

Final-query scores obscure whether an error category was already observed on simpler components or appears only when the complete query is generated.

## Method

Deterministically decomposes reference SQL into executable sub-queries, generates corresponding questions with GPT-4o-mini, and compares predictions with schema and reference structure. Six heuristic categories receive recurrent or emergent labels according to earlier category detection within the path.

## Evaluation

Expands 500 PostgreSQL BIRD-mini cases into 1,384 question–query pairs and evaluates five commercial models with and without prior questions and generations. Reports conditional category probabilities, execution accuracy and result-overlap Soft-F1.

## What the results support

History is generally associated with higher conditional recurrence and lower emergence, with model/category exceptions. Mean final-query execution accuracy changes from 38.28% without history to 37.56% with history, while individual model directions differ.

## Limits and qualifications

Generated questions lack independent human equivalence validation. Rules can flag valid alternative SQL and have not been comprehensively checked against expert judgments. Category recurrence does not identify the same error instance or causal propagation. A single benchmark and changing commercial APIs limit transfer and regeneration; no calibrated uncertainty, ambiguity-handling policy or mitigation intervention is evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides an inspectable trajectory diagnostic for evaluating verification and history-selection hypotheses, with explicit separation of operational labels, semantic correctness and causal explanations.

## Checks against the paper

These are interpretations checked against the source, not verbatim quotations attributed to its authors.

| Claim or inference examined | Original evidence | Location | Assessment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Recurrence quantifies the fraction of final errors caused by earlier errors. | The measured quantity is P(category in final step &#124; category detected earlier), not the reverse conditional; the authors explicitly state that no causal mechanism is identified. | Sections 4 and 7.1, pages 674 and 676; Limitations, page 679 | Retain descriptive category-level association only; neither origin attribution nor causal propagation follows. |
| The deterministic hallucination labels establish semantic incorrectness. | Appendix B flags extra valid columns, clauses, casts and joins relative to one reference, as well as selected wildcard/backtick patterns. Sections 5.1–5.2 disclose unvalidated generated questions and operational rather than human-validated labels. | Sections 5.1–5.2, page 675; Appendices A–B, pages 680–682 | Describe reference-sensitive structural heuristics, not definitive semantic gold labels or a complete error detector. |
| Adding history reduces uncertainty or uniformly improves reliability. | Figures 4–5 show opposite movements for recurrence and emergence and exceptions close to zero; Table 3 contains both positive and negative EX changes. Section 8.1 explicitly says confidence, predictive entropy and epistemic uncertainty are not measured. | Sections 7.3–8.2; Figures 4–5, pages 677–678; Appendix D/Table 3, page 682 | Report the conditional-history pattern and model dependence, without a calibrated-uncertainty or tested-mitigation claim. |
